```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
source("00_requirements.R")
source("01_funct_Data_Processing.R")
```

Loading the Clean Dataset
```{r}
load("22_DataSaving.RData")
head(covid_cleaned)
```

## Plot 1: Histogram of COVID-19 Death Distribution

```{r}

hist(covid_cleaned$COVID.19.Deaths, 
    main = "Distribution of Covid-19 Deaths",
    xlab = "COVID-19 Deaths",
    col = 'darkred',
    breaks = 10)

```

This histogram displays the overall distribution and frequency of COVID-19 Deaths counts across all filters. It highlights that the lower death counts show up as small parts whereas the high deaths show up as a outlier.

## Plot 2: Boxplot of COVID-19 Deaths by Sex

```{r}
boxplot(COVID.19.Deaths ~Sex,
        data = covid_cleaned,
        main = "COVID-19 Deaths by Sex",
        xlab = "Sex",
        ylab = 'COVID-19 Deaths',
        col = c('pink','darkblue'))

```

This box plot compares the median, spread and range of COVID-19 deaths between males and females. It shows variability and highlights whether one group had a higher mortality rate.


## Plot 3: Bar Plot of COVID-19 deaths by age

```{r}

age_totals <- tapply(covid_cleaned$COVID.19.Deaths, covid_cleaned$Age.Group, sum)
barplot(age_totals,
        main = 'Total COVID-19 Deaths by age group',
        xlab = 'Age Group',
        ylab = 'COVID-19 Deaths',
        col = 'darkred')

```

This bar plot shows the total COVID-19 Deaths across age groups only. We are clearly able to intrepret that as someone gets older, they have a higher mortality rate and are more prone to be affected by COVID-19


## Plot 4: Line plot for percentage of all deaths
```{r}
age_combined <- aggregate(
  cbind(COVID.19.Deaths, Total.Deaths) ~ Age.Group, 
  data = covid_cleaned, 
  sum
)

age_combined$Age.Group <- factor(
  age_combined$Age.Group,
  levels = c("Under 1 year", "1-4 years", "5-14 years", "15-24 years",
             "25-34 years", "35-44 years", "45-54 years", "55-64 years",
             "65-74 years", "75-84 years", "85 years and over"),
  ordered = TRUE
)
age_combined <- age_combined[order(age_combined$Age.Group), ]


pct <- (age_combined$COVID.19.Deaths / age_combined$Total.Deaths) * 100


plot(
  pct, 
  type = "b", 
  pch = 20,
  xaxt = "n",
  xlab = '',
  ylab = "COVID-19 % of Total Deaths",
  main = "COVID-19 Share of Total Deaths by Age"
)

axis(1, at = 1:nrow(age_combined), labels = age_combined$Age.Group, las = 2)
```

This line plot shows the percentage of COVID-19 deaths relative to total deaths across the age groups. It portrays how the percentage of deaths change with the age groups.

## Plot 5: COVID-19 vs. Pneumonia Share of Deaths by Age and Sex

```{r}
male <- covid_cleaned[covid_cleaned$Sex == "Male", ]
female <- covid_cleaned[covid_cleaned$Sex == "Female", ]

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(8, 4, 4, 1))

plot(male$covid_pct_of_all, type = "b", ylim = c(0, 12), xaxt = "n",
     xlab = "", ylab = "% of all deaths", main = "Male")
lines(male$pneu_pct_of_all, type = "b", col = "blue")
axis(1, at = 1:11, labels = male$Age.Group, las = 2)
legend("bottomright", legend = c("COVID-19", "Pneumonia"),
       col = c("black", "blue"), lty = 1)


plot(female$covid_pct_of_all, type = "b", ylim = c(0, 12), xaxt = "n",
     xlab = "", ylab = "% of all deaths", main = "Female")
lines(female$pneu_pct_of_all, type = "b", col = "blue")
axis(1, at = 1:11, labels = female$Age.Group, las = 2)
legend("bottomright", legend = c("COVID-19", "Pneumonia"),
       col = c("black", "blue"), lty = 1)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```
These line plots compares how much of all deaths in each age group are due to COVID-19 versus pneumonia. Sex is shown separately to see whether age and sex change which illness accounts for more deaths.

Both COVID-19 and pneumonia related deaths increase as age increases, so age has a visible effect on deaths. Sex does not appear to have a large effect between them, as the two lines follow similar patterns. However, at ages 85 and older, the shares drop for females by about 2-3% in both COVID-19 and pneumonia while males stay near 10%.

## Plot 6: Side-by-Side Bar Plot for Male vs. Female Covid-19 Deaths by Age Group

```{r}
age_deaths_sex <- aggregate(
  COVID.19.Deaths ~ Age.Group + Sex,
  data = covid_cleaned,
  sum
)

age_deaths_sex$Age.Group <- factor(
  age_deaths_sex$Age.Group,
  levels = c("Under 1 year", "1-4 years", "5-14 years", "15-24 years",
             "25-34 years", "35-44 years", "45-54 years", "55-64 years",
             "65-74 years", "75-84 years", "85 years and over"),
  ordered = TRUE
)

death_matrix <- xtabs(
  COVID.19.Deaths ~ Age.Group + Sex,
  data = age_deaths_sex
)

barplot_byside <- barplot(
  t(death_matrix),
  beside = TRUE,
  axisnames = FALSE,
  main = "Count of COVID-19 Deaths by Age Group and Sex",
  xlab = "Age Group",
  ylab = "COVID-19 Deaths",
  col = c("pink", "darkblue"),
  legend.text = TRUE,
  args.legend = list(x = "topleft")
)


axis(side = 1, labels = FALSE)

text(
  x = colMeans(barplot_byside),
  y = -7000,
  labels = levels(age_deaths_sex$Age.Group),
  srt = 45,
  adj = 1,
  xpd = TRUE,
  cex = 0.7
)
```
This side-by-side bar plot shows the count comparison of COVID-19 Deaths based on 11 different age groups while also differentiating between the counts for males vs females. 

This shows a similar trend to Plot 5, with the count of COVID-19 deaths increasing as the age group increases. However, the differences in count between males and females shows that typically males have a significantly higher COVID-19 death count per age group until the oldest age group of 85 years and over, where females have a higher COVID death count than males. 

## Plot 7: Side-by-Side Bar Plot for Male vs. Female Pneumonia Deaths by Age Group

## Plot 8: Side-by-Side Bar Plot for Male vs. Female Total Deaths by Age Group

```{r}
age_deaths_sex3 <- aggregate(
  Total.Deaths ~ Age.Group + Sex,
  data = covid_cleaned,
  sum
)

age_deaths_sex3$Age.Group <- factor(
  age_deaths_sex3$Age.Group,
  levels = c("Under 1 year", "1-4 years", "5-14 years", "15-24 years",
             "25-34 years", "35-44 years", "45-54 years", "55-64 years",
             "65-74 years", "75-84 years", "85 years and over"),
  ordered = TRUE
)

death_matrix3 <- xtabs(
  Total.Deaths ~ Age.Group + Sex,
  data = age_deaths_sex3
)

barplot_byside3 <- barplot(
  t(death_matrix3),
  beside = TRUE,
  axisnames = FALSE,
  main = "Count of Total Deaths by Age Group and Sex",
  xlab = "Age Group",
  ylab = "Total Deaths",
  col = c("pink", "darkblue"),
  legend.text = TRUE,
  args.legend = list(x = "topleft")
)


axis(side = 1, labels = FALSE)

text(
  x = colMeans(barplot_byside3),
  y = -60000,
  labels = levels(age_deaths_sex3$Age.Group),
  srt = 45,
  adj = 1,
  xpd = TRUE,
  cex = 0.7
)
```
This side-by-side bar plot shows the count comparison of Total Deaths based on 11 different age groups while also differentiating between the counts for males vs females. 

This graph shows similar discrepancies between male and female deaths as Plots 5 and 6, but for the oldest age group the significantly higher female death count can larger be attributed to COVID-19 over Pneumonia based on the prior side-by-side bar plots.
